title: Felix and the Wolf Anew
premise: Sebastian Reyes, a mercenary bound to a silent god and trapped in a valley where magic cannot follow, has spent years hiding from the world that sold their soul to the court beneath the mountain. When the old gods stir awake and one of them—the Wolf—answers Sebastian's prayers at last, staying invisible becomes impossible: the god's return marks them for every power hunting the newly woken divine. With a runaway priestess, a debt-ridden ferryman, and the ghost of the brother they failed, Sebastian must cross the falling long winter to steal back their soul before the court beneath the mountain seals its gates until spring. They succeed at terrible cost—Sebastian gives up the god's protection to free the other souls sold alongside theirs—and end the book not as a mercenary or a servant, but as the founder of a household of strays who owe nothing to any law or any god but each other.
about_author: C. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk ballads about bargains gone wrong before turning to fiction. They live in a drafty house full of maps and write stories about people the law forgot.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgot
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A routine escort job through the valley where magic dies reveals someone has been praying at the boundary stones—and something answered. Sebastian feels their old oath twitch like a scar. Emotional beat: wary contentment cracking open; the past knocking.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered Out of Order
chapters.summary: Priestess Odile Vane's POV. Fleeing her order after a god spoke through her mid-sermon, Odile crosses into the valley seeking the famous silence—and finds a mercenary whose brand burns when she prays nearby. Beat: desperate hope meeting stubborn denial.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Left
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Wolf, Sebastian's silent patron god, manifests in a dream-hunt and names what was taken: Sebastian's soul, sold by their own mother to the court beneath the mountain to buy the valley's protection. Beat: betrayal reframing an entire life.

chapters.title: A Ferryman in Debt
chapters.summary: Tomas Bell's POV. The ferryman who smuggles people across the valley line owes the mountain court three favors, and collectors have come for the first: bring them the branded mercenary. Beat: guilt and calculation; Tomas chooses to warn instead of deliver.

chapters.title: Leaving Is a Kind of Dying
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian crosses the boundary for the first time in twelve years; magic floods back, including the soul-debt mark on their skin, now visible to every tracker in the province. Beat: vertigo, grief, and the first taste of freedom that costs.

chapters.title: The Order of the Quiet Mouth
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Pursued by her former sisters, who believe silencing gods is holy work, Odile bargains with Sebastian: her knowledge of the mountain roads for passage out of the order's reach. Beat: two liars learning to trust.

chapters.title: Winter Comes Down Like a Verdict
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The long winter begins early—weeks of dark, snow that erases roads, and courts sealing their doors. The party shelters in a drowned chapel where the Wolf speaks plainly: reach the court before the gates close at solstice. Beat: dread and resolve.

chapters.title: The Brother Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In the chapel, Sebastian meets the ghost of Mateo, the brother who died the night their mother made the bargain—a ghost bound to the soul-debt, who has been following Sebastian for years. Beat: devastating tenderness; grief given a voice.

chapters.title: Roads That Owe Us Nothing
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The second favor comes due: the collectors demand Tomas sabotage the party or forfeit his daughter, who lives in the court's service. He fakes the sabotage badly. Beat: love against duty, and the cost of half-measures.

chapters.title: The Market of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In a winter fair held inside a frozen waterfall, the party trades for passage—and Odile finds her order waiting, offering to erase her heresy if she delivers the god-touched mercenary. Beat: temptation dressed as forgiveness.

chapters.title: What We Steal From Ourselves
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Odile confesses the offer; instead of rage, Sebastian asks her to take it—then watches her burn her own vows rather than betray them. Beat: found family cemented in refusal.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. They descend through mines full of prayer-scraps into a glittering underworld where souls are currency and the Queen of the Long Winter keeps ledgers older than gods. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Posing as a debtor, Sebastian reads their own entry: their soul was collateral, and the valley's protection expires when the ledger closes at solstice—their mother sold a whole town. Beat: the personal wound becoming communal.

chapters.title: The Daughter Below
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas finds his daughter Ilsa, alive, serving as the Queen's record-keeper—and discovers she stayed willingly, because the court keeps its promises when no one else does. Beat: bitter reconciliation; loyalty questioned from within.

chapters.title: A Theft Planned in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The plan forms: during the solstice closing ceremony, every debt in the ledger must be read aloud, and a read debt can be contested by anyone willing to stand surety. Beat: hope sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: The Silence Sells Itself
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Queen offers Sebastian a private deal: keep your soul, leave the others, and the valley stays protected forever. Sebastian sees their mother's choice mirrored back at them. Beat: the book's moral crux.

chapters.title: Solstice
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The gates begin to close; the ceremony of debts begins; Odile contests the ledger publicly, Tomas spends his final favor, and Ilsa turns the records against her Queen. Beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Surety
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. To void the ledger, someone must stand surety for every soul in it. Sebastian offers the only thing they hold: the Wolf's protection, their god's claim upon them, surrendered. The Wolf accepts the loss like a father letting go. Beat: sacrifice as love, not martyrdom.

chapters.title: When Gods Grieve
chapters.summary: Mateo's POV (the ghost). Freed with the other souls, Mateo chooses to stay behind a moment longer to bar the gate against the Queen's pursuit, buying the living their head start. Beat: the brother finally protecting Sebastian; farewell without bitterness.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The flight through the collapsing court and up the winter roads, carrying freed souls who have nowhere to go. Ilsa chooses her father over her Queen. Beat: exhaustion, laughter, the strange lightness after ruin.

chapters.title: An Unprotected Valley
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. They return to find the valley's magic-protection dead with the ledger—and the townsfolk furious, then listening, then helping raise walls and wards of their own making. Justice outside the law, built by hand. Beat: reckoning turned into beginning.

chapters.title: Felix and the Wolf Anew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, coda. Spring. The household of strays—Odile, Tomas, Ilsa, and the returned—keeps a shrine with no god in it, though sometimes paw prints appear in the ash. Sebastian signs the new valley charter 'Felix': lucky, happy, free. Beat: quiet joy; a life chosen, not owed.
